# S↔K Vocabulary — `documentType` contract (KS-388 / KS-134)

The two platforms exchange a `documentType` value in two **different** places with two
**different** meanings. This document is the single reference for what each field accepts,
decided 2026-07-08 (KS-388; consumer ticket on S: PS-138).

## 1. Originate — `POST /api/documents` → `documentType`

**What it is:** the document's *type* — an entry in the platform's admin-managed
document-type catalogue (`GET /api/document-types`; admin CRUD at `/api/admin/document-types`).

**Validation:** dynamic, against the registered catalogue — **not** a hardcoded enum
(a static enum would fight the admin CRUD that creates new types at runtime).
Implemented in the gateway's `enforceDocumentTypeRules` (`services/api-gateway/src/services/enforcement.ts`):

- Catalogue **has** registered types + value not in it (by `code` or `id`, code match
  case-insensitive) → **400 `UNKNOWN_DOCUMENT_TYPE`**.
- Catalogue **empty** (never seeded, or Redis TTL expiry) → validation is not configured;
  the value passes through unchanged (historical behaviour — this guard is what keeps a
  fresh, unseeded boot from rejecting every creation).
- No `documentType` sent → passes; originate defaults it to `DOCUMENT`.

**Seeded contract types** (in `SEED_DOCUMENT_TYPES`, `services/api-gateway/src/routes/admin.ts`):

| Code | Purpose |
|---|---|
| `SSD_DOCUMENT` | Fixed value Platform-S sends on originate (`CardanoAnchorService.cs`). Friction-free: no verification levels / MFA / approval, so connector-scoped S calls are never gated. **S: keep sending this unchanged.** |
| `DOCUMENT` | Originate's fallback for typeless creations. Friction-free. |
| `DEGREE`, `LICENSE`, `REFERENCE`, `TRANSCRIPT`, `VCERT`, `RECOMMENDATION` | Demo/business seed types (pre-existing). |

## 2. Flat anchor — `POST /api/anchors` → `metadata.documentType`

**What it is:** the *lifecycle verb* being anchored. Platform-S routes verbs that have no
dedicated K endpoint through this flat path with the verb here.

**Validation:** frozen to the **KS-134 master S↔K verb vocabulary** as a strict enum.
The vocabulary K *advertises* is `LIFECYCLE_VERBS`; what K currently *accepts* is
`ACCEPTED_LIFECYCLE_VERBS` — the canonical list plus any transitional alias still inside
its deploy window (both in `services/anchoring/src/anchorSchema.ts`). Out-of-vocabulary →
**400** (Zod schema reject), never silently anchored.

```
upload · watermark · sign · declare · share ·
rights-assign · rights-unassign · rights-reassign ·
share-revoke · share-permission-change ·
share-recipient-change · share-expiry-change · share-token-rotate · share-resend ·
share-attach-consent ·
delete · rename · view · download ·
protect · unprotect · restore
note · certified · verified
```

- **`declare` was `certify` until 2026-08-26 (KS-661).** Terminology only — what the verb
  does, anchors and records is unchanged; the rename frees `certify` as a word for the
  certification family. The **certification storage names are deliberately untouched**:
  `POST /api/certifications/issue`, the `certifications` table, `certified_at`,
  `isCertified` all keep their names (PS-612 assumes they do not move), and
  `services/originate/src/routes/certifications.ts` still writes `action: 'certify'` to
  `action_provenance` — that row records the certification family's own act, not the S↔K
  lifecycle verb. **Existing stored rows are left as test residue, not migrated** (Kam's
  ruling, 2026-08-24): everything anchored so far is testnet, so there is no real-world
  provenance to falsify, and Platform-S mirrors the same call for its 21 UAT
  `DocumentTransaction` rows so PS-287's chain-match sees both sides agree.
  **`certify` is still ACCEPTED as a transitional alias** (`TRANSITIONAL_LIFECYCLE_VERBS`)
  so an un-upgraded S keeps anchoring across the deploy window — an out-of-vocabulary verb
  400s the *whole* anchor, not just the label (PS-499), which is why **K deploys first and
  S switches afterwards**. The alias is **not permanent**: once every S instance emits
  `declare`, empty that tuple and `certify` stops being accepted. Say so explicitly here
  when it happens (KS-661 step 3).
- `share-attach-consent` is the **PS-458 attach-consent** verb, added 2026-07-30 (KS-534):
  the sender's consent, for ONE share, to email an **uncontrolled copy** of the document as
  an attachment — a release Secuura cannot revoke, expire or access-log. It is the consent
  that is recorded, not a change to the document (non-mutating; `contentHash` stays the
  current blob). **Unlike every other `share-*` verb it is not governed by live share-link
  state** — revoking or expiring the link does not recall the emailed copy, so the consent
  stays true whatever becomes of the link. One row per document per share submit; never
  reused between shares.
- The four `share-*-change`/`share-token-rotate`/`share-resend` verbs are the PS-235
  share-edit set, added 2026-07-10 (KS-415). Accepted on the flat path while S still
  routes fallback verbs here; once S's PS-123 router re-point lands they travel via
  `/lifecycle-events` (§3) instead.

Notes:

- The field stays **optional** — K's own internal originate→anchoring calls send no
  `metadata.documentType` and are unaffected.
- **`metadata.timestamp` is the CLIENT-ASSERTED event time (KS-555, added 2026-08-04):**
  ISO 8601 (offset allowed; non-ISO → **400** — a garbage string is a caller error, never
  silently anchored, same posture as the verb enum). It is anchored as **`occurredAt`**,
  normalised to UTC, alongside K's own anchoring `timestamp` — so provenance carries both
  "when it happened" (S-asserted) and "when it hit chain" (K-asserted), labelled, with no
  trust conflation. Motivation: after UAT's 31-Jul drain, replayed July events all carried
  a 31-Jul anchoring stamp and nothing else. Optional; anchors without it read back
  `occurredAt: null`.
- **`metadata.identityCommitment` is Platform-S's opaque keyed identity commitment
  (KS-721, added 2026-08-31):** `<label>.v<N>:<64 lowercase hex>` — an HMAC-SHA256 over an
  actor's identity snapshot bound to the event id, computed on S (PS-711). Max 128 chars;
  malformed values → **400**, same posture as the verb enum and `metadata.timestamp`.
  Anchored **verbatim** (an opaque token must not be normalised — re-encoding it breaks the
  equality check S performs), read back on `GET /api/anchors/verify/:hash` as
  `metadata.identityCommitment`. Optional; anchors without it read back `null`.
  - `vN` names the **S-side key version**. The field is admitted under KS-240 only because
    S committed on KS-721 to **destroying that key version on erasure** — which turns the
    anchored value from a permanent, permanently-checkable pseudonym into something
    permanently unverifiable. K validates **shape only**: that the value is non-identifying
    is Platform-S's assertion, not a property K can prove.
- ~~`POST /api/anchors` is an S-integration endpoint and is deliberately **not** in the
  public OpenAPI spec.~~ **Stale — corrected 2026-08-31 (KS-721).** The claim was written on
  2026-07-08 (KS-388, `fa6a8ef73`) and stopped being true on 2026-07-30, when KS-480 §10②b
  (`72987ffe6`) registered the route in `anchoring.openapi.ts`. `POST /api/anchors` **is**
  published today — it is one of the spec's 289 paths — so it is fuzzed by Schemathesis and
  visible to Akto like any other operation, and a change to `FlatAnchorRequest` is a change to
  the published contract. Corrected here rather than left, because the next person reading this
  line would conclude a new request field needs no spec declaration.

## 3. Lifecycle events — `POST /api/documents/{id}/lifecycle-events` → `action` (KS-387)

**What it is:** the generic endpoint for the verbs that have **no dedicated K route**.
It records a **non-mutating** lifecycle row (bytes unchanged → attaches to the *current*
document via `parent_document_id`, no version fork) and returns a resolvable `anchorId`
via the same shared emitter as `/share`, `/transfer-custody`, `/revoke` (KS-319).

**Validation:** strict enum (`LIFECYCLE_EVENT_ACTIONS` in
`services/originate/src/lifecycleActions.ts`). Out-of-set → **400** with the accepted list.

```
rights-unassign · share-revoke · share-permission-change · rename · delete · restore ·
share-recipient-change · share-expiry-change · share-token-rotate · share-resend ·
share-attach-consent · protect · unprotect
note · certified · verified
```

- Verbs **with** dedicated endpoints (`share`, `transfer-custody`, `revoke`, `declare`,
  `sign`, upload/version) are deliberately rejected here — use their own routes;
  accepting them twice would double-record lifecycle rows. (`declare`'s dedicated route is
  `POST /api/certifications/issue`, whose name is unchanged by the KS-661 rename. Note this
  list has never contained `certify` either — `LIFECYCLE_EVENT_ACTIONS` never accepted it,
  so the §3 path needs no change for KS-661.)
- `delete` / `restore` implement the **KS-389 decision**: S's owner-local, recoverable
  soft-delete records here — **never** as K `/revoke`, which is a terminal global
  withdrawal.
- `rename` is accepted now; S sends it once PS-64 (filename stability) and its net-new
  `TransactionAction.Rename` land.
- The four **PS-235 share-edit verbs** (`share-recipient-change`, `share-expiry-change`,
  `share-token-rotate`, `share-resend`) are accepted here since KS-415 (2026-07-10) —
  they are exactly the KS-387 shape: non-mutating, attach to the current document, no
  dedicated K endpoint. Payload shapes are documented on PS-235.
- `share-attach-consent` (**PS-458**, accepted here since KS-534, 2026-07-30) — same
  KS-387 shape, with the one semantic difference noted in §2: the consent is independent of
  live share-link state.
- `protect` / `unprotect` (**PS-499**, accepted since KS-556, 2026-08-04) — S's document
  edit/delete-guard toggle. Real S lifecycle events, exactly the KS-387 shape (non-mutating,
  attach to the current document). Also added to the flat-path vocabulary in §2 alongside
  `restore` (already accepted here since KS-389) so S can stop omitting `documentType` on
  the fallback path for all three.
- `note` / `certified` / `verified` (**Stuart's Flow project, KS-1172 + KS-1173, 2026-09-15**) — `note`: a user
  attached a short plain-text note to a document; the text stays on S and the payload carries only
  `noteSha256` / `noteLength` (a content commitment, never the text). `certified`: the Certify FLOW completed
  (every required declaration made and the organisation's signature applied — one row per flow, after its
  `declare` and `sign` events; not the transitional `certify` alias). `verified`: the Verify FLOW completed —
  every required verifier confirmed; verifier identities as DID / credential references only. All three
  non-mutating, exactly the KS-387 shape; also added to the flat-path vocabulary in §2.
- Read side: `GET /api/documents/{id}/lifecycle-events` (tenant-scoped, newest first).
- Events persist in `document_lifecycle_events` (migration 037).
- **⚠ PII caveat for payload authors:** `payload` is stored as **unencrypted JSONB** and is
  since KS-537 (2026-07-31) encrypted at rest (platform keyring, AAD-bound per event) and
  covered by GDPR erasure (the subject's email is deep-pseudonymised inside stored
  payloads). The caller contract is unchanged by that hardening: send a count or an opaque
  reference (`recipientCount`, a rights-profile id, a hash), **never verbatim addresses or
  names** — lifecycle events are retained audit records, and encryption is defence in
  depth, not permission.

## Related S↔K contracts

Ownership, identity and tenancy between the platforms (per-Organisation `sk_` connector
keys, on-behalf-of attribution, org→tenant binding) are governed by
[S-K-OWNERSHIP-CONTRACT.md](./S-K-OWNERSHIP-CONTRACT.md) (KS-480 / PS-319).

## Changing the vocabulary

Growing/shrinking either set is a **cross-platform contract change**:

1. Agree with S first (PS-138 is the S-side consumer ticket).
2. Update `LIFECYCLE_VERBS` (+ its pinning unit test in
   `services/anchoring/src/__tests__/anchorSchema.test.ts`) or the seed catalogue.
3. Update this document in the same change.
